summary: Ice surface of each year 2016 to 2026 on the 3D strip: two swisstopo elevation models (2012, 2023), and an elevation-band lowering shape borrowed from Rhone for the years between and beyond. A model, not a measurement, except where a survey lies.

anchors.survey: GLAMOS volume-change table (release 2025, all-combinations file) lists this surface as source "sa3d-2018" with date_end 20129999: survey 2012, day unknown. Image strips over the strip in 2012 (swisstopo layer ch.swisstopo.lubis-bildstreifen): 2012-08-18 TLM (100 % of ice cells, computed), 2012-08-27 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (100 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published; the model puts the whole edition on one day.
anchors.placed_at: 2012-08-27 (a day a strip was flown, taken from the pair of flown days with the lowest ICESat-2 rmse (3.23 m); ties within 0.05 m go to the GLAMOS date if it is among them, else to the strip covering most ice. Chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent. A2 was then set to the flight day of its lidar (see A2))

anchors.source: swissALTI3D newest edition (2025 edition; swisstopo), which equals the swissSURFACE3D lidar of 2023 over the ice
anchors.survey: GLAMOS names 20230823 (is-stand). The edition equals the swissSURFACE3D raster of 2023 on the ice (median absolute difference under 0.05 m on every one of the 22 tiles with ice, computed). GPS times of the point clouds of 22 of these tiles (100 % of the 2023 ice cells, computed) were read: 20 tiles were flown entirely on 2023-07-11, tile 2656-1159 on 2023-07-11 (99.9 % of its points) and 2023-08-10 (0.1 %), and tile 2655-1160 (119 ice cells, 0.5 % of the ice) on 2023-07-11 (71.2 %) and 2023-08-10 (28.8 %); the day of A2 is 2023-07-11 (computed from the GPS times).
anchors.placed_at: 2023-07-11 (the flight day of that lidar; not a strip day: the best strip day of the year, chosen by the pair rule, lay 40 days later)

shape: Between two anchors the surface follows the lowering of each elevation band, from snow-off (1 May plus Bw/|Bs| x 153 d, melt even from 1 May: an assumption) to 30 September. GLAMOS has no band balance for Unteraargletscher (no row in the elevation-bin file; the point files hold stake readings of 1997 to 1999 only, none after the first survey). The band balance is that of Rhone (release 2025, bins from 1700 to 3700 m covering 100 % of the ice, computed; non-commercial); it only decides how the change between two surveys is spread, the size comes from the surveys. Tried on the same ICESat-2 shots (rmse, computed): Corbassiere 3.00 m (covers 75 %: not eligible); Rhone 3.12 m; the borrowed line 3.26 m (covers 75 %: not eligible); Findel 3.48 m (covers 2 %: not eligible); Aletsch 3.55 m; the lowest among the candidates covering at least 98 % of the ice is used. 2026: the Rhone bands are estimated (computed): each band regressed on the glacier-wide Bw and Bs of Grosser Aletsch (2005 to 2025) and evaluated at the Aletsch 2026 values read from the GLAMOS figure (Bw +751.6, Bs -3790.0 mm w.e., about +-100 mm w.e.). Beyond the last anchor (2024 to 2026) the rate of the last segment is applied to the measured 2023 surface, from the anchor difference smoothed over about 100 m (the raw difference carries noise and made 2024 to 2026 rough). The ground outside the 2023 outline stays at its 2023 height and no fade is applied, so a step grows along the outline (median lowering of the ice cells next to it 1.8 m in 2024, 3.1 m in 2025, 4.6 m in 2026, computed). Every cell stays between its two anchors or, outside them, within 2.5 times the lowering of its band at the nearest anchor.

validation.icesat2: ICESat-2 ATL06 v007: 1,912 shots on 2023 ice in 15 granules (July to October, slope under 20 degrees, quality 0, h_li_sigma under 1 m, inside the physical envelope). rmse 3.23 m over all years, bias +0.25 m (model minus shot), leave-one-granule-out: the A1 and A2 days are chosen on the other granules and the held-out granule is scored; with the days used 3.12 m. Per year (leave-one-granule-out): 2019 1.53 m (1 shot); 2020 3.09 m (108 shots); 2021 2.86 m (781 shots); 2022 0.96 m (206 shots); 2023 1.89 m (323 shots); 2024 3.18 m (146 shots); 2025 5.27 m (347 shots). Years without summer shots are not checked.
validation.datum: The usual plane fitted on stable ground scattered by 2.21 m (NMAD, 5895 shots), more than 2 m, so heights are corrected with an offset only, fitted on 696 shots on gentle stable ground (slope under 15 degrees) within 1.5 km of the ice (NMAD 0.82 m).
validation.not_checked: The split of the loss between years is an assumption (even melt from snow-off to 30 September); ICESat-2 scores years with shots, not each year step. 3 of 63 ASTER AST14DEM scenes (NASA LP DAAC, July to October 2016 to 2026) passed the gate (rock NMAD at most 15 m, at least 300 rock and 200 ice cells) in 2019, 2020; ASTER is rough, so only differences of a few metres mean something. No stake check: the GLAMOS point files of Unteraargletscher (release 2025) hold readings of 1997 to 1999 only, none after the first survey (2012).

bed: Ice surfaces are not allowed below the bedrock: swissBEDROCK (swisstopo, 10 m; under glaciers swissALTI3D minus a modelled ice thickness, GLAMOS 2020) is the floor.
not_used: Airborne research DEMs and TanDEM-X series: the RAGMAC set covers Aletsch only (read); a first search for others is recorded in the source ledger of this glacier, and none was used; no radar surface was used. Years before 2016 are not modelled: older pictures use the 2016 surface.
licences: swisstopo open government data (swissALTI3D, swissSURFACE3D, image-strip footprints). The GLAMOS balances of Rhone and volume change: non-commercial (file headers). ICESat-2 (NASA, ATL06) and ASTER AST14DEM (NASA LP DAAC): used for checking only; the ASTER terms of use were not read. GLAMOS ice thickness release 2020 (radar beds, CC BY 4.0 per the landing page) and swissBEDROCK (swisstopo open government data): used for the ice bed checks.
caveat_2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance of the Rhone bands estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch (computed regression): provisional; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)

bed.lead: Three checks on Unteraargletscher (all computed here, not source figures). The bed is the rock under the ice. "Radar bed" is the radar's own bed elevation (the survey surface minus the measured thickness, from the GLAMOS release); "model bed" is swissBEDROCK, which under glaciers is swissALTI3D minus a modelled GLAMOS ice thickness.
checks:
1 · Radar bed against model bed

At the 1,393 radar cells (20 m, median of the points in a cell), how far apart are the two beds?

Median −2.1 m over all cells, but it depends on the survey: −2.1 m (2002, 973 cells), −2.1 m (2012, 420 cells). Spread (standard deviation) 16.2 m in 2002, 3.7 m in 2012; over all cells 66 % are within 10 m and 96 % within 30 m.

Reading: the 2012 survey agrees closest (94 % of its cells within 10 m) and the 2002 survey least (53 %). This is not a validation: the model bed was made from these same surveys (GLAMOS 2020 model, Grab et al. 2021), and at the survey lines it is the measured bed.

2 · One survey against another

Where two surveys covered the same spot, how well do they repeat?

Only 22 spots (25 m cells) have two survey dates (2002 and 2012: 22). The beds implied by the two surveys differ by a median −15.6 m (later minus earlier) with a standard deviation of 15.7 m; 32 % agree within 10 m.

Reading: few spots, so this is a hint and not a measure of the surveys.

3 · Ground that is ice free now

Radar points where the newest swissALTI3D shows ground, not ice: the exposed ground is the bed.

98 points (96 from 2012, 2 from 2002) on 3 flight profiles, ice about 60 m thick:

2012
Radar bed − ground now−2.6 m (−2.7 to −2.3)
Model bed − ground now+1.5 m (+0.9 to +2.2)

Median, in brackets the middle half (years with too few points are not shown). 2 % of the points have the radar bed above the ground now.

Light blue: ice in the SGI2023 outline; dashed: the SGI2016 outline, the ice the model was made for. The points lie in the strip between the two outlines, kept 30 m clear of both. bed.read:
What this supports

  • At the margins the radar bed lies 2.6 m below the exposed ground and the model bed 1.5 m above it (medians of the points of 2012).

What it does not show

  • Few places: the 98 points lie on 3 flight profiles, at the margins where the ice is about 60 m thick; deeper ice may behave differently.
  • No error band: the GLAMOS release has no uncertainty maps for the model bed, and swissBEDROCK's band under glaciers is about 0. Lakes, debris and the margin position (a few metres) were not screened.

How the points were chosen

  • In the 3D strip, at least 30 m outside the SGI2023 outline and 30 m inside the SGI2016 outline, so the model had ice there; newest swissALTI3D, slope at most 20°. With up to 30°: 99 points; with a 50 m margin: none; with 100 m: none.

notes.uncertainty: Median over the ice of 2023, red whisker the 90th percentile (computed). The two swisstopo surveys carry 1.27 m (rmse of the 323 shots of 2023). swisstopo quotes 0.5 m below 2000 m and 1 to 3 m above (as quoted by Bannwart et al.), so the true value may be larger on a tongue this high. Between and beyond the surveys the error grows with the size of the change (factors 0.37 and 0.93), calibrated on the same ICESat-2 shots, so it is not independent; where a year has shots it is not below their rmse. Years without shots (2016, 2017, 2018) rest on the formula alone. 2026 has no value on the chart: it is an estimate (its balance is estimated from a figure for Aletsch), and its map in the viewer adds 25 % of its increment (median 6.1 m).
notes.sharing: Solid: the loss between two surveys is shared over the years by an elevation-band balance borrowed from Rhone (GLAMOS has none for Unteraargletscher; chosen on ICESat-2 among the candidates that cover the ice). Dashed: extrapolated beyond the last survey (2026 with an estimated balance). Not used: measured years.
notes.independent: ICESat-2 also chose the survey days of both anchors and calibrated σ, so it is not independent (rmse is leave-one-granule-out). ASTER scenes are checks only (3 of 63 scenes usable; usable years: 2019, 2020). There are no stake readings for Unteraargletscher after its first survey. Click a year for the numbers.

page.viewerText: The yearly surfaces in 3D with a year slider, the same viewer as for Aletsch. Switch on ICESat-2 shots (what the model was checked against) and hover a shot for its values; the bed and uncertainty colours are in the Colour menu. About 10 MB, loaded when you press the button.
page.mapcap: The model area = the 3D strip (outlined in black), as set in the walkthrough. Blue: ice inside the 2023 outline, about 13.4 km² (computed, 20 m cells). Red dashed: every cell modelled as ice, including ground that was ice at the 2012 survey, about 14.4 km² (computed). The 1,912 ICESat-2 shots used for the checks are shown in the 3D viewer (last section). Every modelled ice cell lies within 1 km of an ICESat-2 shot used for the check. Pictures of years before 2016 use the 2016 surface.
page.icesatNote: Also used to choose the survey days of both anchors, so not an independent check; the rmse is leave-one-granule-out (the days are chosen on the other granules).
page.asterNote: For scale: each used scene has a stable-terrain NMAD of 9.7 to 13.2 m (computed) (no used scene lies within 25 days of the 2023 anchor), so differences of a few metres are within ASTER's own scatter. rms = spread of the scene values of the year. Check only, not in the fit.
